principles: Known space has disagreements, regulation, labor conflict, commercial rivalry and historical resentment without requiring a single galactic government or central villain.
Political jurisdictions overlap with trade standards; species identity does not define political allegiance.
Most conflicts encountered by freight operators should create practical choices: cost, access, delay, risk, legality or relationships.

issues.name: Frontier Resource Claims
issues.description: Governments, survey crews, investors and settlers disagree about when discovery creates an enforceable extraction right.

issues.name: Native Biosphere Protection
issues.description: Morrow and future living worlds create tension between scientific access, contamination control and commercial pressure.

issues.name: Port Automation and Labor
issues.description: Automation lowers handling costs but can destabilize communities whose economies formed around dock work.

issues.name: Salvage Title
issues.description: Outer-space recovery law is standardized imperfectly. Ownership of abandoned ships and cargo can remain disputed.

issues.name: Standards Lock-in
issues.description: Concord standards simplify commerce but established manufacturers benefit disproportionately when new standards resemble existing products.

issues.name: Talos Growth
issues.description: Residents, mining interests and infrastructure authorities disagree over how quickly a temporary boom camp should become a permanent governed settlement.
